explanation_text: Voltage insuced [latex]=\int_{0}^{1}E_m \cdot dt[/latex] (where [latex]E_m[/latex] is induced electric field) Since, Volatage induced =1 V So,  [latex]E_m[/latex] = 1 V/m As we know, [latex]E_m=\bar{V} \times \bar{B}[/latex] where, V= (radius of path) x (angular velocity) [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{1V}{m} &=(V \times 1 \; \text{Tesla}) \\ V&=1 \; m/sec \\ V&= r \times \omega =1 \; m/sec\\ \text{Since, } r&=1m, \; \text{So }\omega =1 \; \text{rad/sec} \end{aligned}[/latex] Now from this we get [latex]\begin{aligned} \omega &=2 \times \pi \times \frac{N}{60}=1 \; \text{rad/sec}\\ N&=\frac{30}{\pi}=9.55 \; \text{revolutions per minute} \end{aligned}[/latex]
